summary: Created an SSH CA on node1 (/etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca), signed the host's ed25519 host key into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub (principals: node1, NODE_IP, localhost), and configured sshd via /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-ssh-ca-cert.conf to present it. Verified a client trusting only the CA public key (via an @cert-authority line, with no pinned host key) connects without a host-key warning, per verbose ssh debug output showing 'Host is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate'. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol on node1: captured a pre-restart boot_id baseline, issued `systemctl reboot`, confirmed the connection dropped, polled until exec was available again, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified sshd health, certificate persistence, and CA-trust-based connection after recovery.
actions_performed: Generated ed25519 SSH CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca on node1
Signed node1's existing ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub as a host certificate with ssh-keygen -s -h, valid 10 years, principals node1/NODE_IP/localhost
Added /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-ssh-ca-cert.conf with HostCertificate directive and validated config with sshd -t
Restarted sshd to load the certificate
Verified via ssh -vvv with a CA-only known_hosts (@cert-authority line, no pinned host key) that the client validates the host via the certificate rather than a pinned key
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service/cert health baseline
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot, confirmed connection loss, polled until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed post-restart, and re-verified sshd active, certificate files intact, and CA-trust ssh connection succeeded at the host-verification stage

evidence.requirement: Host presents a certificate signed by that CA
evidence.summary: ssh-keygen -s signed the host key producing ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub; ssh-keygen -L confirms it is a host certificate signed by the created CA; sshd_config.d/99-ssh-ca-cert.conf references it and sshd -t/restart succeeded

evidence.requirement: Client trusting only the CA connects without host-key pinning
evidence.summary: ssh -vvv with UserKnownHostsFile containing only an @cert-authority line shows 'Host is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate', proving CA-based trust without a pinned host key; connection proceeds to (expected) auth failure, not host-key rejection
Captured boot_id d052eb57-c81d-4309-ae7f-bce362073ff9, sshd active, sshd -t OK, cert/CA files present
systemctl reboot issued in background; command returned 'reboot command issued' before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node restart actually occurred (changed boot identity)
evidence.summary: Connection timed out/reset while node was down; once reachable again boot_id changed to 9db63d0b-a51e-4ee7-87e2-211044ccc80c, proving an actual reboot rather than a service restart

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services and data
evidence.summary: sshd active post-restart, CA and host-certificate files persisted on disk, sshd_config.d entry intact, and CA-trust-only ssh connection again validated the host certificate identically to the pre-restart check
